what: re-home the opt-in persistent fetch refspec to sdd:init as its own CR. install-refspec was cut from this CR at spec-gate rounds 2-4: it added no capability over sync, was the engine's only mutation of a user's git config, and contradicted the node's own reach-is-never-implicit rule -- a contradiction that drifted the reach rule into a different file each round. It is not abandoned. sdd:init already exists to onboard optional repo-scoped conveniences and already asks consent before writing operational config, which gives the CI cost (once installed, a diverged store ref makes UNRELATED git fetch calls exit 1) a place to be disclosed at the point of choice.
evidence: spec-gate rounds 2-4; the judge classified the drift REGRESSING rather than converging, and it stopped the round the contradicting clause was removed

what: two of the three sync 'both refs differ' scenario tests do not discriminate the mechanism they appear to test. The impl-judge deleted the destination-less fetch outright and only the fast-forward test failed; publish-ahead and refuse still passed. Two confounds: git clone of a LOCAL PATH hardlinks the whole object store regardless of ref filtering, so the fixture's object is already present without any fetch; and isAncestor's blanket catch-to-false makes a missing-object error indistinguishable from a genuine not-an-ancestor answer, so both land on refuse. Not a live bug -- the specified behavior does hold in the unmutated code, confirmed by direct execution -- but two tests give false confidence they would catch a regression in object delivery. Judge's suggested fix (assert git cat-file -e <remoteHead> fails in the clone before syncStore runs) needs the fixtures moved to clone --no-hardlinks first, or the precondition cannot hold.
evidence: impl-gate round 2 mutation testing: removing mission-graph.mts's destination-less fetch fails 1 of 3 delta-reachable tests, not 3

what: sync's ancestry check now runs against a fetched-but-unreferenced object, which is prune-eligible immediately -- git prune --expire=now -n lists it and fsck flags it dangling. The old scratch ref was a real GC root for the duration of the check. Default gc --auto's two-week grace period protects it in practice; only an explicit aggressive prune racing the same sub-second window would not. No frozen scenario models this, and the window is narrower than the concurrent-collision case the change eliminated, so it was accepted rather than fixed. Revisit if the fleet ever runs gc --prune=now on a shared tree.
evidence: impl-gate round 2, reproduced in throwaway repos; FETCH_HEAD confirmed NOT to be a gc reachability root
